'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Tigray War]]
**[[Ethiopian Prime Minister]] [[Abiy Ahmed]] announces that [[Eritrean troops]] will withdraw from the [[Tigray Region]] after pressure mounted on them on accusations of [[human rights in Ethiopia|human rights]] violations. The announcement came after a meeting with [[Eritrea]]n [[President of Eritrea|President]] [[Isaias Afwerki]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/ethiopian-pm-eritrean-troops-to-leave-tigray/a-57009807 (DW)]
*[[War in Donbas (2014–2022)|War in Donbass]]
**Four [[Ukrainian Ground Forces|Ukrainian troops]] are killed and two others are wounded in a [[Separatist forces of the war in Donbass|separatist]] rocket attack on a military position in the [[Donetsk Oblast]]. It is the worst loss of life in a single attack for Ukrainian forces since 2019. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/03/26/kyiv-says-four-soldiers-killed-in-a-bombing-in-eastern-ukraine (Euronews)]
*[[Colombian conflict]]
**A [[car bomb]]ing in front of the City Hall of the municipality of [[Corinto, Cauca]], [[Colombia]], wounds 16 people and is attributed to [[drug trafficking]] [[terrorism in Colombia|terrorism]]. [https://www.elperiodico.com/es/internacional/20210327/heridos-coche-bomba-colombia-16-11617891 (''El Periódico'')]
*At least four people are killed in [[Chittagong]], [[Bangladesh]], when police open fire at protesters during a [[demonstration (political)|demonstration]] against a visit by [[government of India|India]]n [[Prime Minister of India|Prime Minister]] [[Narendra Modi]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/26/anger-in-bangladesh-as-indias-modi-attends-50th-independence-day (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Belarus in the Eurovision Song Contest 2021]], [[2020–2021 Belarusian protests]]
**[[Belarus]] is disqualified from the [[Eurovision Song Contest 2021|Eurovision Song Contest]] after their entry [[Galasy ZMesta]]'s song "[[Ya nauchu tebya (I'll Teach You)]]" was deemed inappropriate by the [[European Broadcasting Union]] due to its "political [[subtext]]". Galasy ZMesta has been known for mocking the [[2020–2021 Belarusian protests|protests]] against [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-56540236 (BBC News)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Transport in Romania]]
**The [[Bucharest Metro]] stops operating as a result of a [[strike action|strike]] by the [[trade union]] of the metro. The [[government of Romania|government]] and [[Metrorex]] condemn the strike as illegal. [https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/actualitate/protest-spontan-la-metrou-niciun-tren-nu-circula-vineri-dimineata-toate-statiile-au-lacatul-pus-1474355 (Digi 24)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[Sohag train collision]]
**At least 19 people are killed and 185 others are injured after two [[trains collide]] in [[Sohag Governorate|Sohag]], [[Egypt]]. Passengers triggered the [[Emergency brake (train)|emergency brakes]] on the first train; a second train following on the same track was not stopped. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/27/egypt-buries-train-crash-dead-toll-revised-to-19 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Suez Canal obstruction]]
**The [[Suez Canal Authority]] accepts an offer from the [[United States Navy]] to deploy an assessment team of dredging experts to assist in efforts to remove the stranded [[container ship|Ultra Large Container Vessel]] ''[[Ever Given]]''. The [[Suez Canal]] has now been blocked for four consecutive days. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/03/26/politics/us-navy-suez-assistance/index.html (CNN)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maharashtra]]
*****The [[Maharashtra]] [[Government of Maharashtra|state government]] imposes a night curfew beginning on March 28, due to an increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases. [https://www.indiatoday.in/coronavirus-outbreak/story/maharashtra-night-curfew-across-state-from-sunday-rising-covid19-cases-uddhav-thackeray-1784087-2021-03-26 (India Today)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mongolia]]
****[[Mongolia]] reports a record 437 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 6,332. [https://akipress.com/news:656036:_b_Mongolia_reports_a_record_high_437_daily_cases_of_coronavirus_/b_/ (AKIPress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] reports a record 9,838 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, with the country surpassing 100,000 total active cases. This also brings the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 702,856. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/coronavirus-cases-philippines-march-26-2021 (Rappler)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus]]
****The [[Second Anastasiades government|government]]'s spokesman Kyriacos Koushos tests positive for COVID-19. [https://cyprus-mail.com/2021/03/26/coronavirus-government-spokesman-tests-positive/ (Cyprus-Mail)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hungary]]
****[[Hungary]] reports a record 11,265 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 614,612. [https://bbj.hu/economy/statistics/figures/11-823-new-coronavirus-cases-registered-in-hungary (Budapest Business Journal)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] introduces a mandatory hotel [[quarantine]] for travellers from 33 high-risk countries, mostly in [[South America]] and [[Africa]]. Travellers from these countries will be required to quarantine for 14 days at a government-designated facility. [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/ireland/irish-news/ireland-s-mandatory-hotel-quarantine-regime-comes-into-force-1.4520747 (''The Irish Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Poland]]
****[[Poland]] reports a record for the third consecutive day of 35,143 new confirmed cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 2,189,966. [https://www.polskieradio.pl/395/7989/Artykul/2704496,Poland-reports-new-daily-record-of-35143-COVID19-cases (Polskie Radio)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a record 18,132 new confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1,614,707. [https://www.kyivpost.com/ukraine-politics/covid-19-in-ukraine-record-18132-new-cases-326-new-deaths-18738-new-vaccinations.html (''Kyiv Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kenya]]
****[[President of Kenya|President]] [[Uhuru Kenyatta]] announces a [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] and curfew from 8:00 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. local time in [[Nairobi]], [[Kiambu]], [[Machakos]], [[Kajiado]] and [[Nakuru]] counties beginning tomorrow due to an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20210326-kenya-slaps-five-counties-on-lockdown-bracing-for-third-wave-of-covid-19 (RFI)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mauritania]]
****[[Mauritania]] begins a [[vaccination]] campaign against COVID-19 after receiving 500,000 doses of the [[Sinovac]] [[CoronaVac]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] from [[China]]. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/mauritania-begins-covid-19-vaccination-campaign/2189322 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Brazil]]
****[[Brazil]] reports a record 3,650 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://riotimesonline.com/brazil-news/miscellaneous/covid-19/brazil-sees-record-3650-new-covid-19-deaths-health-ministry-says/ (''The Rio Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia]]
****The [[Colombia]]n National Institute for Drug and Food Surveillance grants emergency use authorization for the single-dose [[Johnson & Johnson COVID-19 vaccine|Johnson & Johnson]] vaccine. [https://www.elperiodico.com/es/internacional/20210326/colombia-autoriza-vacuna-johnson-johnson-covid-11614332 (''El Periódico'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Mexico]]
*****[[Governor of New Mexico|New Mexico Governor]] [[Michelle Lujan Grisham]] receives her first dose of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine]]. [https://www.sfgate.com/news/article/New-Mexico-governor-gets-initial-vaccine-shot-at-16056932.php (''San Francisco Chronicle'')]
****The [[Presidency of Joe Biden|Biden administration]] announces that the [[United States]] is expected to receive 11 million doses of the vaccine produced by [[Johnson & Johnson]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/health-coronavirus-whitehouse/update-1-us-to-distribute-11-million-johnson-johnson-covid-19-shots-next-week-white-house-idUSL1N2LO1L2 (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin]]
****[[Wisconsin]] confirms their first cases of the [[Lineage P.1]] and [[501.V2 variant]] of [[SARS-CoV-2]]. [https://www.wbay.com/2021/03/26/wisconsin-health-officials-confirm-south-africa-covid-19-variant/ (WBAY-TV)] [https://madison.com/wsj/news/local/govt-and-politics/first-case-of-brazilian-covid-19-variant-found-in-wisconsin/article_3d421b4d-4f58-50b5-9e37-9475c0f8a03f.html (Madison.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Arizona]], [[501.V2 variant]]
****[[Arizona]] reports its first case of the 501.V2 variant, which was originally detected in [[South Africa]]. [https://www.azcentral.com/story/news/local/arizona-health/2021/03/26/arizona-has-confirmed-two-cases-south-african-coronavirus-strain/7021506002/ (''The Arizona Republic'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Maine]], [[Lineage P.1]]
****[[Maine]] reports its first case of the Lineage P.1 variant, which was originally detected in [[Brazil]]. [https://www.centralmaine.com/2021/03/26/state-reports-253-new-covid-19-cases-highest-daily-total-since-early-february/ (Central Maine)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Cross-Strait relations]]
**[[Taiwan]] reports the largest ever incursion into its [[air defence identification zone]] by [[People's Liberation Army Air Force]] warplanes. The fleet of Chinese aircraft, including [[Xian H-6]] [[strategic bomber]]s and [[Shenyang J-16]] fighter jets, flew south of the island over the [[Bashi Channel]], according to a statement from Taiwan's Defence Ministry. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-taiwna-china-security/taiwan-reports-largest-ever-incursion-by-chinese-air-force-idUSKBN2BI24D?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Ivory Coast|Ivorian]] [[List of heads of state of Ivory Coast|President]] [[Alassane Ouattara]] names [[Patrick Achi]] as [[List of heads of government of Ivory Coast|Prime Minister]] following the death of [[Hamed Bakayoko]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/3/26/ivory-coasts-ouattara-names-confidant-achi-as-pm (Al Jazeera)]
